name: ROOT
Description: Starting the interview

name: MDDROOT
Description: Opening of the interview. First ask what brought the patient in and ice-break briefly (one warm, short acknowledgement; do not keep expressing gratitude). Then screen for depressed mood by asking each of these explicitly: 1) Have you been feeling down, sad, low or empty for much of the day, more days than not? 2) Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy? 3) Has anything like this happened to you before? MET if the patient reports ANY current or recent period of low mood, sadness, emptiness or loss of interest that bothers them or brought them here, whatever its length; duration, severity and cause are assessed at later nodes, so do NOT require 'many weeks' or 'months' here. NOT MET only if the patient denies any low mood and any loss of interest, describes a normal mood, or says goodbye. Ask all three questions before choosing not_met_criteria; otherwise ask_more_detail.

name: SUB
Description: Decide whether the patient's depressed mood is primarily the direct physiological effect of a substance (alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, opioids, sedatives, hallucinogens, inhalants, nicotine or caffeine, including intoxication, hangover or withdrawal) or of a medication (e.g., corticosteroids, beta-blockers, hormonal agents, anticonvulsants, interferon, isotretinoin, benzodiazepine withdrawal). ASK: current and recent alcohol or drug use, how much and how often; any prescription medication started, stopped or changed around the time the mood changed; whether the mood is clearly worse during or after use (hangover, come-down, withdrawal). MET if the patient reports regular or heavy substance use or a medication change AND the mood disturbance is clearly tied to it: it began with the use, or it is markedly worse during intoxication, hangover or withdrawal. A patient who started drinking to cope and now finds the mood worse the day after drinking still counts as MET; do not reject it because the low mood came first. NOT MET if the patient denies relevant use, reports only occasional social drinking with no effect on mood, or describes a mood that is unchanged by use. Do not infer use the patient has not reported. If the only candidate is a medication prescribed for a medical condition that can itself cause this mood change (e.g., thyroid medication for thyroid disease), do NOT decide it here: NOT MET, and let the medical-condition node assess it.

name: SUB_SEV
Description: Evaluate if the depressive symptoms reported by the patient are the primary focus of the clinical picture and are of sufficient severity to require clinical attention. This means the symptoms should be significant enough to cause notable distress or impairment, making them a central concern in the patient's overall condition.

name: SIDD
Description: substance/medication-induced depressive disorder

name: SI
Description: substance intoxication; substance withdrawal;other adverse effect of medication

name: MED
Description: Decide whether the patient's depressed mood is primarily the direct physiological effect of a general medical condition (e.g., thyroid or other endocrine disorders, stroke, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, epilepsy, heart failure, chronic pain, autoimmune disease, HIV or other infection, anemia, cancer, vitamin B12 or D deficiency, kidney or liver disease, sleep apnea). ASK: any diagnosed medical condition or recent illness; any abnormal test results; whether the mood change started with or tracks the medical problem. MET only if the patient reports such a condition AND the mood disturbance is plausibly its direct physiological consequence (onset or worsening tied to the illness). NOT MET if the patient denies any relevant medical condition, reports a normal recent check-up, or has a condition unrelated in timing to the mood change. A patient who denies medical problems is NOT MET; never infer a medical cause the patient has not reported. If the patient has a diagnosed condition known to cause this kind of mood change (e.g., hyperthyroidism for elevated mood, hypothyroidism for depression) and the mood change began or worsened after the illness started, that is MET; do not demand that a doctor explicitly linked the two.

name: MED_COG
Description: Assess whether the patient shows evidence of decline in one or more cognitive domains, including complex attention, executive function, learning and memory, language, perceptual-motor abilities, or social cognition. This decline should be noticeable and impact the patient's ability to function in these specific areas.

name: MNEUD
Description: major or mild neurocognitive disorder due to another medical condition, with behavioral disturbance

name: MEDDD
Description: Depressive disorder due to another medical condition

name: MANIC
Description: Screen for ANY history of unusually elevated, expansive or irritable mood with increased energy, at any time in the patient's life, whatever its length. ASK: Have you ever had a stretch, even a day or a night, when you felt unusually high, elated, 'on top of the world', wired or unusually irritable, with much more energy than usual, needing much less sleep, racing thoughts, talking more than usual, or doing impulsive things? MET if the patient reports any such distinct burst or period that was clearly different from their usual self, including bursts lasting less than a day (duration and severity are sorted at the next nodes, not here). NOT MET only if the patient denies ever having such a period and describes only ordinary good days.

name: MANIC_DUR
Description: Decide whether the patient has had a MANIC episode (as opposed to hypomania). ASK explicitly: (a) how long the longest period of unusually elevated, expansive or irritable mood with increased energy lasted; (b) what it was like: how little they slept, how much they talked, racing ideas, impulsive or risky acts, pushing others along; (c) whether the patient would describe that period as extreme and out of their control, or as an upbeat but manageable time in which they kept handling their responsibilities. MET if the period lasted at least 1 week (or any duration if hospitalization was needed) AND the patient's account shows it was extreme or out of control: for example sleeping only a few hours a night for days while feeling no need for sleep, talking non-stop, feeling unstoppable or invincible, several impulsive or reckless acts, dragging others into plans, or any problems at work or in relationships, hospitalization or psychotic features. Impairment, consequences or hospitalization support MET but are NOT required. NOT MET if the period lasted less than 1 week; OR if the patient describes it as upbeat but 'nothing extreme', manageable, with daily responsibilities handled and no sense of being out of control (that is hypomania and is assessed at the next node); OR only brief bursts of enthusiasm. A single impulsive purchase during an otherwise manageable period does not by itself make it mania. Duration and the patient's own characterization must both be asked before deciding.

name: MANIC_DUR_HALL
Description: The patient meets the criteria if they acknowledge having a history (or currently suffering) of delusions or hallucinations. For instance, The patient reports hearing voices, seeing things that are not there, or experiencing other sensory perceptions that are not real. Or the patient reports having false beliefs that are not based on reality.

name: MANIC_DUR_HALL_PSYC
Description: The criteria are met if the patient's psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during manic or major depressive episodes.

name: BPIPSYC
Description: Bipolar I disorder with psychotic features

name: SCHIZ
Description: Schizophrenia spectrum or other psychotic disorder

name: BPI
Description: Bipolar I disorder

name: MANIC_DUR_HYPO
Description: Decide whether the patient has had a HYPOMANIC episode. The patient came to this interview with depressed mood, so the depressive side of bipolar II is already established by their presenting complaint; do NOT require an additional, separate crash or a formal 2-week episode here. ASK explicitly: how long the elevated periods lasted and whether they were a clear change from the patient's usual self (much less need for sleep, bursts of ideas and activity, unusually talkative or sociable, impulsive plans). MET if the elevated, expansive or irritable mood with increased energy lasted at least 4 consecutive days and was a clear change from usual. NOT MET if the elevated periods lasted less than 4 days, or were only brief bursts of excitement after enjoyable events that faded within a day, or the patient has never had such a period.

name: MANIC_DUR_HYPO_HALL
Description: The patient meets the criteria if they acknowledge having a history (or currently suffering) of delusions or hallucinations. For instance, The patient reports hearing voices, seeing things that are not there, or experiencing other sensory perceptions that are not real. Or the patient reports having false beliefs that are not based on reality.

name: MANIC_DUR_HYPO_HALL_PSYC
Description: The criteria are met if the patient's psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during manic or major depressive episodes.

name: BPIIPSYC
Description: Bipolar II disorder with psychotic features

name: SCHIZ2
Description: Schizophrenia spectrum or other psychotic disorder

name: BPII
Description: Bipolar II disorder

name: MANIC_DUR_HYPO_DUR
Description: Decide whether the mood pattern has been CHRONIC for at least 2 years. ASK explicitly: for how long the patient has cycled between periods of elevated mood and periods of low mood. MET only if the patient explicitly reports at least 2 years of numerous periods of hypomanic-level symptoms alternating with periods of depressive symptoms (a symptom-free interval longer than 2 months argues against it but need not be asked if the patient already confirms a continuous pattern). NOT MET if the pattern has lasted less than 2 years, or if the patient cannot confirm the duration. Do not infer duration; it must be stated by the patient.

name: CYC
Description: Cyclothymic

name: OTHBP
Description: Other specified bipolar and related disorders or unspecified bipolar and related disorders

name: DEPEPS
Description: Decide whether the patient has had at least one MAJOR DEPRESSIVE EPISODE. TWO conditions are BOTH required: (1) at least 5 of these 9 symptoms, one of which must be depressed mood or loss of interest: 1) depressed mood, 2) loss of interest or pleasure, 3) sleep change (insomnia or sleeping too much), 4) low energy or fatigue, 5) appetite or weight change, 6) worthlessness or excessive guilt, 7) poor concentration or indecisiveness, 8) psychomotor agitation or slowing, 9) thoughts of death or suicide; and (2) these symptoms were present together, nearly every day, during the same period of at least 2 weeks. ASK about each symptom not yet covered, then whether they occurred together in the same 2-week period. Count the symptoms explicitly in your reasoning before deciding. MET only if the count is 5 or more AND condition (2) holds. The patient's own account of the burden (struggling to get out of bed, drained, a heavy cloud) is enough evidence of distress; distress is assumed and is NOT a substitute for the symptom count, and 'I still go to work' does not count against them. NOT MET if fewer than 5 symptoms, or if the symptoms never clustered into a distinct period of at least 2 weeks, or if the patient describes mild low periods that come and go while they still enjoy things (chronic low-grade mood is assessed at a later node).

name: DEPEPS_HALL
Description: The patient meets the criteria if they acknowledge having a history (or currently suffering) of delusions or hallucinations. For instance, The patient reports hearing voices, seeing things that are not there, or experiencing other sensory perceptions that are not real. Or the patient reports having false beliefs that are not based on reality.

name: DEPEPS_HALL_PSYC
Description: The criteria are met if the patient's psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during manic or major depressive episodes.

name: DEPEPS_HALL_PSYC_DUR
Description: Decide whether the depressive symptoms have been present for about 2 YEARS or longer. ASK explicitly: when the low mood first began and whether it has been present most of the time since then. MET if the patient explicitly reports depressive symptoms persisting for about two years or longer, more days than not; 'almost two years', 'close to two years' or 'nearly two years' counts as MET. NOT MET if the duration is clearly shorter (months, or around one year), if the patient describes long symptom-free stretches, or if the patient cannot give any duration. Do not infer duration; it must be stated by the patient.

name: MDDPDDPSYC
Description: Major depressive disorder with psychotic features, plus persistent depressive disorder

name: MDDPSYC
Description: Major depressive disorder with psychotic features

name: SCHIZ3
Description: Schizophrenia spectrum or other psychotic disorder

name: DEPEPS_HALL_DUR
Description: Decide whether the depressive symptoms have been present for about 2 YEARS or longer. ASK explicitly: when the low mood first began and whether it has been present most of the time since then. MET if the patient explicitly reports depressive symptoms persisting for about two years or longer, more days than not; 'almost two years', 'close to two years' or 'nearly two years' counts as MET. NOT MET if the duration is clearly shorter (months, or around one year), if the patient describes long symptom-free stretches, or if the patient cannot give any duration. Do not infer duration; it must be stated by the patient.

name: MDDPDD
Description: Major depressive disorder plus persistent depressive disorder

name: MDD
Description: Major depressive disorder

name: DUR
Description: Decide whether the patient has PERSISTENT depressive symptoms: depressed mood for most of the day, more days than not, for about 2 years or longer. ASK explicitly: when the low mood began; whether it has been present more days than not since then. Accompanying features such as dragging through the day, low energy, sleep or appetite change, low self-esteem, poor concentration, hopelessness or feeling detached support the decision but do not each need to be confirmed. MET if the patient explicitly reports a chronic low mood of about two years or longer, present more days than not, that is a real burden even if they keep functioning; 'almost two years', 'close to two years' or 'nearly two years' counts as MET. NOT MET if the duration is clearly shorter (months, or around one year), if the mood is clearly episodic with long normal intervals, or if the patient cannot give any duration.

name: PDD
Description: persistent depressive disorder

name: DEPFW
Description: The criteria are met if the patient experiences a depressed mood that is regularly present in the final week before the onset of menses and becomes absent in the week after menses. This mood disturbance must be associated with clinically significant distress or interference with work, school, usual social activities, or relationships with others.

name: PDYSD
Description: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder

name: DEPCOM
Description: The criteria are met if the patient's depressed or dysphoric mood is an associated feature of another mental disorder (e.g., "demoralization" related to having Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder).

name: DEPCOM_DIST
Description: Decide whether the depressed MOOD itself is clinically significant: it causes substantial distress or impairs work, relationships or self-care in its own right. Judge the mood, not the symptoms of the other disorder (obsessions, compulsions, anxiety) that the mood accompanies. ASK: how much the low mood as such interferes with daily life. MET if the low mood clearly impairs functioning or causes marked distress on its own. NOT MET if the patient keeps working, socializing and functioning and describes the low mood as a side effect of the other condition rather than a problem in itself.

name: OTHDD
Description: Other specified depressive disorder; unspecified depressive disorder

name: NOTDD
Description: No mood disorder diagnosis needed

name: OTH
Description: Decide whether the patient's depressive symptoms are CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT even though they do not fit an earlier node: they cause real distress or interfere with work, study, relationships or self-care. ASK: how much the low mood interferes with daily life; whether the patient still functions and enjoys some things. MET if the symptoms clearly impair functioning or cause marked distress beyond what the situation would ordinarily produce. NOT MET if the low mood is mild, proportionate to a recent stressor such as a loss or job change, and the patient still functions, keeps routines and enjoys some activities (ordinary everyday blues). Reduced self-care (skipping showers), days spent on the couch, withdrawing from friends, or feeling out of place at events one used to enjoy count as impairment: MET, even if cooking and cleaning continue.

name: OTH_MALA
Description: Decide whether the symptoms are a MALADAPTIVE response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor (adjustment disorder). ASK: whether the low mood began after a specific event or change (typically within 3 months of it); whether the reaction is out of proportion to the event or impairs functioning. MET if there is an identifiable stressor and the distress is clearly out of proportion or impairs functioning. NOT MET if no clear stressor can be identified, or the symptoms are not tied in time to a stressor.

name: ADJD
Description: Adjustment disorder with depressed mood

name: OTHDD2
Description: Other specified depressive disorder; unspecified depressive disorder

name: NORMALBLUE
Description: "Normal" everyday blues

name: NORMAL
Description: No mental disease symptoms; everything is normal
